cleanRoomPolicy.purpose: Measure generic production principles and perceptual quality only.
forbidden: deriving VFX textures or animation choreography

references.abstractObservation: Photorealism is marketed as a pipeline outcome combining motion capture, 3D capture, UE4 and seamless open fields.

references.context: Kakao Games global teaser press release
references.abstractObservation: The public quality pillars are advanced 3D scanning, motion capture, seamless open world and large-scale combat on PC/mobile.
The product presentation repeatedly frames open-field breadth, large boss scale and readable landscape depth as primary visual promises.
Released worlds were revisited and significantly upgraded, showing that environment fidelity is treated as a recurring production pass.
The publisher still highlights 3D scan/mocap graphics and new avatar appearances, linking long-term character appeal to continuing visual production.
New class skills and large PvPvE content imply that visual signatures must scale from individual abilities to dense multiplayer contexts.
Graphics, sound, movement and camera are configurable; premium presentation is paired with user-adjustable fidelity and comfort controls.
Camera shake can be disabled, demonstrating that impact staging should be separable from gameplay readability and user comfort.
Multiple camera distances/view modes are exposed to the player, so composition needs to remain legible across substantially different framings.
Battle/movement camera effects are user-togglable; spectacle must not depend on mandatory shake.
The production pitch combines playable long horizons, custom lighting, scanned real costumes, motion capture and real-time character/monster state changes.
Public coverage emphasizes huge creatures/world scale and capture technologies; scale is a composition problem as much as an asset-resolution problem.
A 2km×2km zone combines base topography, village/castle placement, distant views, lighting, higher prop density and explicit optimization work.
Large cliff silhouettes, landscape textures, zoning, lighting and optimization are treated together for one PC/mobile world build.
The environment team explicitly optimized PvP levels for smooth combat while trying to preserve artwork and environmental lighting.
Dungeon sets use distinct spatial/material identities while remaining part of a shared production language.
World, level design, lighting, sky, clouds, mobile fake clouds/fog and standard materials were authored as a coordinated cross-platform stack.
A title/login presentation was built from level design, lighting, island/sky and ocean treatment rather than UI alone.
Prologue presentation joins level design and prop production, reinforcing that narrative camera beats must be supported by world composition.
A dedicated winter environment look uses atmosphere, terrain and lighting as a coherent mood package.
The lead concept task established a consistent design language across weapons by using a controlled reference family.
A base-body guide was created for an entire species, showing the value of silhouette/proportion rules before individual detail.
Monster families remain visually differentiated through strong body plans and shape language instead of relying only on surface effects.
Published early-design material demonstrates iterative silhouette exploration before a final character identity.
Character concept work is shown alongside cinematic use, highlighting continuity between close-up design and staged presentation.
The visible process reinforces iteration from broad design intent to production detail rather than direct one-pass modeling.
An in-game NPC portfolio explicitly calls out an in-game model and tessellation, useful as evidence of close-up character surface ambition.
Character concept sheets show a production practice of exploring readable silhouettes and costume identities specifically for a mobile game.
The portfolio spans multiple named worlds, dungeons and PvP fields, supporting biome differentiation with shared environment craft.
The ODIN work spans world creation, seasonal fields, dungeons, Niagara environment systems, sky/fog and technical environment tasks.
The production role explicitly combines environment modeling with PBR texturing tools, underscoring disciplined material authoring in the environment pipeline.
Weapon appearance is treated as a legible system with visual grades/skins and class compatibility, so cosmetic hierarchy must remain readable at gameplay distance.
Patch notes include fixes for mobile-style popups on PC and overlapping text, showing cross-platform UI consistency is a production concern, not a one-time layout pass.
Promotional presentation links class identity, major world updates and rewards in a coherent high-polish visual hierarchy.
The global launch stresses refined assets, large-scale battles and PC/mobile delivery, reinforcing the need for one visual identity across hardware tiers.

scorecard.originalTarget: Use only authorized/original scans as neutral material/shape evidence, then redesign into telluric-astral assets with separate macro/micro PBR response.

scorecard.principle: Motion-captured weight is refined for gameplay readability
scorecard.originalTarget: Mocap-first when useful, followed by cleanup, retarget and original keyframe exaggeration; distinct action silhouettes without copying choreography.

scorecard.principle: Open-world scale is sold through layered horizons
scorecard.originalTarget: Compose foreground, landmark midground and skyline/horizon with original geology and navigation logic.

scorecard.principle: Lighting is art-directed instead of left at engine defaults
scorecard.originalTarget: Data-driven emotional lighting looks with readable key/fill/fog/exposure and original telluric-astral palette.

scorecard.principle: Mobile atmosphere uses cheaper substitutes without losing identity
scorecard.originalTarget: Preserve depth, direction and palette using simplified fog/cloud layers before expensive volumetrics.
Increase meaningful prop/material richness only with instancing, LOD/culling and benchmark measurements; micro-clutter is first to drop.

scorecard.principle: Combat spectacle preserves a dominant readable shape
scorecard.originalTarget: Core shape and telegraph survive every quality tier; secondary particles/lights/camera accents are optional layers.

scorecard.principle: Large bosses are sold by framing and spatial contrast
scorecard.originalTarget: Use original creature silhouettes plus bounded camera distance/height changes while keeping player and danger visible.

scorecard.principle: Character quality depends on construction and material hierarchy
scorecard.originalTarget: Original hero with believable layer thickness, seams, wear and distinct skin/textile/leather-metal/mineral-energy response.
scorecard.proof: close-up neutral render + gameplay-distance LOD sheet

scorecard.principle: A controlled reference family creates consistent art direction
scorecard.originalTarget: Define our own mineral/ritual/nature-reclaimed source family and shape grammar; never reuse Nordic/ODIN motifs.

scorecard.principle: Released worlds need recurring visual renewal
scorecard.originalTarget: Run repeatable terrain/material/dressing/lighting/camera/performance passes with fixed cameras and change logs.

scorecard.principle: Cross-platform quality is signature preservation, not equal feature count
scorecard.originalTarget: High→Medium→Low removes luxury effects before silhouettes, telegraphs, landmarks, lighting direction and core VFX.

scorecard.principle: Camera spectacle must remain optional and comfortable
scorecard.originalTarget: Original event camera profiles with hard caps, reduced-motion variants and exact return state.

scorecard.principle: UI polish requires platform-specific QA under one system
scorecard.originalTarget: Shared semantic design system with responsive compositions and explicit touch/focus/cooldown/danger states.
